.qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r7/rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/references/quality-checks.md section '2 · instruction_preserves_natural_human_voice' (Verify/Defect lines 13-15) plus neighbouring A-block checks
evidence: Skill procedure (quality-checks.md:14-15): verify sentence variety, contractions, occasional terse fragments; defect = uniform cadence, marketing gloss, perfectly parallel bullets, or voice change between instruction.md and notes. instruction.md reads as a real team lead talking: first-person/colleague framing ('Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day?' :1; 'Several of us have it open at once, so the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled' :1; 'tell me who' :3; 'I often move several candidates together' :3; 'layout and names are yours' :11; 'How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call' :13). Contractions present (nobody's, don't x2, it's, mustn't — :1,:11,:13). Sentence length varies from short ('Candidates sign in too.' :9; 'Interview has a limited number of places per job.' :3) to long compound sentences; no numbered acceptance list or bullets in the brief. Grep for marketing gloss (seamless|robust|delve|leverage|ensure|comprehensive|intuitive|streamline) over instruction.md and both notes: zero hits. hireops_rules.md keeps the same owner voice ('These are the working rules for HireOps, our recruiting workspace... what we care about is that the workspace behaves the way this note says' :3-5; 'Where drafts are kept is yours' :174-175; 'Each application has one conversation between our side and the candidate' :127); its tables and bullets are the natural form for a role/stage rules sheet and the bullets are not mechanically parallel (e.g. :47-53, :69-73). integration.md lines 1-14 are byte-for-byte the template's integration.md (template-controlled), lines 16-19 are a plain operational addendum. Minor observations, not defects for this row (P3 at most, no grading impact): (a) rules §8 'Runtime file paths' (:196-202) shifts to an impersonal ops-boilerplate register ('It runs as an unprivileged user and may launch a writable copy... Resolve bundled UI and seed files relative to the entry or module directory'); (b) spelling mixes British 'honour/honouring' (instruction.md:13) with American 'honoring' (integration.md:7, template text) and 'Honor' (hireops_rules.md:201) — a hint of multiple authors that row 3 may weigh; (c) ragged over-long lines at hireops_rules.md:99, :112, :173 (169/141/154 chars vs ~105 wrap elsewhere) suggest later insertions — a hygiene matter for row 3, not voice. None makes the prose robotic or LLM-polished. Adversarial check: this row grades prose only, so no broken app can pass or conforming app fail via it; the only way voice harms a model is by ambiguity, which belongs to row 6. No runtime evidence is required for this row; no Oracle/model/portal score is claimed.
